Sulfites (often spelled **sulphites** ) are sulfur-based compounds—typically sulfur dioxide (SO₂)—found naturally in all wine as a byproduct of yeast fermentation and often added by winemakers as a preservative.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESnQEBxCJF13PRtNbqTGDlfFra_2vkCZCqw4SnPLR59_iR5BbsX1h56tsXZZQ0FyL_0RmlJW6cZ32uxTaKtcBF0poM9Aid4lVVEgUs-_WzpS6o2dxV9tg8iacE93ImzStn52rTqCcerFajF9eSlwc-RI_2e5qQrqtz6GOzPNi88nR482UAGGV2a4U5zCXICW4COvMZVkRsPgRH1hmZJAXZ)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESggEBxCJF1wsA4_D3nWC3xzmq4R8HxFyuHZDXlpFcmMf8Elqk28PlpOqNttNJ1QOCt3sZhnONWu-8ZaRV0Sb6IWLhxZbc9wdHKsCCxL1-8SqOfp_F3oriITiPmmK3YpAYVPJKGIbiV7z2_7nXDReDuVqqbzFmtuS7_HDfl9uYPj1GV0GO)[[3]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESawHEIkXXeclU773glZR6gk8NabNGiTjbQ1a2W2OkOILM3w79rvtbXai7I-cL4134CGGrU4AyTh1m_CMLbzQZAb0KPc-sKeSh0uIc3-lKccbuK9DVDQYs2jurqz-JQMq5pkG2zYa293tOjUcd)

### Why Winemakers Use Sulfites

- **Prevent oxidation:** They bind to oxygen so wine does not turn brown or taste stale or like vinegar.
- **Stop spoilage:** They act as an antimicrobial agent to block unwanted bacteria and wild yeasts.
- **Preserve freshness and ageability:** They protect flavor, color, and shelf life.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESZgHEIkXXz-5q9SyjAos242u0cr26ulfhj3XyJ2TZNrvS4HSUV54TeP20hqexqNXAX70r9tOSrKgeKoB1pzf5ZA_0B_oJbu9TdCLm2vGPFjCYiznhxg1ke24RE4FNvfxEJvrIBt3V2w)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESlwEBxCJF1-bs4a6jXQ4SotTWFxL-5r1N1IKnqHxI0eeXWvyQW61FOBXuxVMYsK4xyLlZhSX-oCimWZKxIkyovqFXJNOLqg1rBO4Xe3RILIswNEa1_Uf_KDFMJgtxAc_dppU_S-G90KIBBk-S8Nxopu5xz8nSI_np6LbGSYsHeRhJzav5PwOUIJuQqOSFP9XhSTPXcHqaaTyV)[[3]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESawHEIkXXeclU773glZR6gk8NabNGiTjbQ1a2W2OkOILM3w79rvtbXai7I-cL4134CGGrU4AyTh1m_CMLbzQZAb0KPc-sKeSh0uIc3-lKccbuK9DVDQYs2jurqz-JQMq5pkG2zYa293tOjUcd)[[4]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESZgHEIkXXxAmNuLDYQWRcKDO31CqSuGzUPoqnYpE-UPipdZyMYrDkPxDTDUT7WIDwcABBOYWh0GjptN4wLeC7ZtBL2hBl3DhY1CQ2c5wHMSve2izn-xuBZo5Ge7jl2BKAorBpjwCzXg)[[5]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESnQEBxCJF13PRtNbqTGDlfFra_2vkCZCqw4SnPLR59_iR5BbsX1h56tsXZZQ0FyL_0RmlJW6cZ32uxTaKtcBF0poM9Aid4lVVEgUs-_WzpS6o2dxV9tg8iacE93ImzStn52rTqCcerFajF9eSlwc-RI_2e5qQrqtz6GOzPNi88nR482UAGGV2a4U5zCXICW4COvMZVkRsPgRH1hmZJAXZ)

### Levels and Labeling

- **All wine contains some sulfites:** Even wines labeled "no added sulfites" or "natural" contain small amounts made naturally during fermentation.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESggEBxCJF1wsA4_D3nWC3xzmq4R8HxFyuHZDXlpFcmMf8Elqk28PlpOqNttNJ1QOCt3sZhnONWu-8ZaRV0Sb6IWLhxZbc9wdHKsCCxL1-8SqOfp_F3oriITiPmmK3YpAYVPJKGIbiV7z2_7nXDReDuVqqbzFmtuS7_HDfl9uYPj1GV0GO)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAEShQEBxCJF1wbgkeIPnze0_JVEOu5TbgNPZpCloe5WoQ2PgsrLyEAHz7V7APWaspMIyozC1j5-dPMmDeE4bhZMF3MLYi3RbIy3dY2nB6jZgwW51sa5CvDO-stTUGRg5TN0pYwBWGw8oLn6usBgTf0-7vcV_M6ChM5hdGRpZCa1xEbg7MdJ4vpw)
- **Style differences:** Sweet and white wines generally hold higher sulfite levels than dry or red wines. Many other foods, such as dried apricots, contain far higher concentrations than wine.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESZgHEIkXXy9khoHEt4NE5jdkFek1bNesC4_XAX2QksbzXMBAUgLu835HU4JnjUoW6rebJaCS7tj0zuhELwIiHku24c6NuFpsL6ZMZGpDtUjuyFX1mUz28uh-iGF5rYlKXJkVdPPHfFg)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESggEBxCJF1wsA4_D3nWC3xzmq4R8HxFyuHZDXlpFcmMf8Elqk28PlpOqNttNJ1QOCt3sZhnONWu-8ZaRV0Sb6IWLhxZbc9wdHKsCCxL1-8SqOfp_F3oriITiPmmK3YpAYVPJKGIbiV7z2_7nXDReDuVqqbzFmtuS7_HDfl9uYPj1GV0GO)[[3]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESnQEBxCJF13PRtNbqTGDlfFra_2vkCZCqw4SnPLR59_iR5BbsX1h56tsXZZQ0FyL_0RmlJW6cZ32uxTaKtcBF0poM9Aid4lVVEgUs-_WzpS6o2dxV9tg8iacE93ImzStn52rTqCcerFajF9eSlwc-RI_2e5qQrqtz6GOzPNi88nR482UAGGV2a4U5zCXICW4COvMZVkRsPgRH1hmZJAXZ)[[4]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESzgEBxCJF10EHFlrF-nMewxUn4QyWrbOHHdjq63HXTNl32yfer02HkY1ROmdXr7XSQWYId0wttLoyBuLvdRSsd4PZCWbJEQKDjXTCZ_YvaTyTtGVpDipWUL9Yf5FVmTmJbFU8fULnJJem6IU2x8sqblQa4JkzVhvYJSOmQWw9RZn9aQ4qi8Tumj9MrVJwcKL1dD4Noj_dxyjfJyspz-roYzFbg03OFHg2sLu_GRMbnntd-me3Z6YH6I7fppsRUiJdp7ngQxkqU9LG98uBMA1OQg)
- **Label rules:** In the U.S., wines with **10 parts per million (ppm)** or more must state "Contains Sulfites" on the label.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESYwHEIkXXMNw05EsHKhu93E7-e56DMi1IRNcVxhbpfOuvo5RarThld3ezxwyvxdnU48tp9fnOS7GzsgljByRyJe84FULyO_0xIY2qu_4yPcSOfPdDyyRsA6Adh5XXzq1W-vZ1GQ)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESggEBxCJF1wsA4_D3nWC3xzmq4R8HxFyuHZDXlpFcmMf8Elqk28PlpOqNttNJ1QOCt3sZhnONWu-8ZaRV0Sb6IWLhxZbc9wdHKsCCxL1-8SqOfp_F3oriITiPmmK3YpAYVPJKGIbiV7z2_7nXDReDuVqqbzFmtuS7_HDfl9uYPj1GV0GO)

You can read more about winemaking roles and labeling rules in the [Napa Valley Wine Academy guide to sulfites](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESggEBxCJF1wsA4_D3nWC3xzmq4R8HxFyuHZDXlpFcmMf8Elqk28PlpOqNttNJ1QOCt3sZhnONWu-8ZaRV0Sb6IWLhxZbc9wdHKsCCxL1-8SqOfp_F3oriITiPmmK3YpAYVPJKGIbiV7z2_7nXDReDuVqqbzFmtuS7_HDfl9uYPj1GV0GO) or explore health and food comparisons from the [European Food Information Council (EUFIC)](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESnQEBxCJF13PRtNbqTGDlfFra_2vkCZCqw4SnPLR59_iR5BbsX1h56tsXZZQ0FyL_0RmlJW6cZ32uxTaKtcBF0poM9Aid4lVVEgUs-_WzpS6o2dxV9tg8iacE93ImzStn52rTqCcerFajF9eSlwc-RI_2e5qQrqtz6GOzPNi88nR482UAGGV2a4U5zCXICW4COvMZVkRsPgRH1hmZJAXZ).[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESggEBxCJF1wsA4_D3nWC3xzmq4R8HxFyuHZDXlpFcmMf8Elqk28PlpOqNttNJ1QOCt3sZhnONWu-8ZaRV0Sb6IWLhxZbc9wdHKsCCxL1-8SqOfp_F3oriITiPmmK3YpAYVPJKGIbiV7z2_7nXDReDuVqqbzFmtuS7_HDfl9uYPj1GV0GO)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESnQEBxCJF13PRtNbqTGDlfFra_2vkCZCqw4SnPLR59_iR5BbsX1h56tsXZZQ0FyL_0RmlJW6cZ32uxTaKtcBF0poM9Aid4lVVEgUs-_WzpS6o2dxV9tg8iacE93ImzStn52rTqCcerFajF9eSlwc-RI_2e5qQrqtz6GOzPNi88nR482UAGGV2a4U5zCXICW4COvMZVkRsPgRH1hmZJAXZ)

### Health Effects
For most people, sulfites are harmless and are **not** the main cause of wine headaches (alcohol, dehydration, and other wine compounds are more likely culprits). Sensitivity is uncommon and affects a small percentage of people with asthma, who may experience breathing symptoms.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESawHEIkXXeclU773glZR6gk8NabNGiTjbQ1a2W2OkOILM3w79rvtbXai7I-cL4134CGGrU4AyTh1m_CMLbzQZAb0KPc-sKeSh0uIc3-lKccbuK9DVDQYs2jurqz-JQMq5pkG2zYa293tOjUcd)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESggEBxCJF1wsA4_D3nWC3xzmq4R8HxFyuHZDXlpFcmMf8Elqk28PlpOqNttNJ1QOCt3sZhnONWu-8ZaRV0Sb6IWLhxZbc9wdHKsCCxL1-8SqOfp_F3oriITiPmmK3YpAYVPJKGIbiV7z2_7nXDReDuVqqbzFmtuS7_HDfl9uYPj1GV0GO)[[3]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESYwHEIkXXMNw05EsHKhu93E7-e56DMi1IRNcVxhbpfOuvo5RarThld3ezxwyvxdnU48tp9fnOS7GzsgljByRyJe84FULyO_0xIY2qu_4yPcSOfPdDyyRsA6Adh5XXzq1W-vZ1GQ)[[4]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESnQEBxCJF13PRtNbqTGDlfFra_2vkCZCqw4SnPLR59_iR5BbsX1h56tsXZZQ0FyL_0RmlJW6cZ32uxTaKtcBF0poM9Aid4lVVEgUs-_WzpS6o2dxV9tg8iacE93ImzStn52rTqCcerFajF9eSlwc-RI_2e5qQrqtz6GOzPNi88nR482UAGGV2a4U5zCXICW4COvMZVkRsPgRH1hmZJAXZ)Are you asking because you get **headaches** or **allergy-like symptoms** after drinking wine, or are you shopping for **low-sulfite** or **no-added-sulfite** bottles?

items.title: Health Effects
items.text: For most people, sulfites are harmless and are not the main cause of wine headaches (alcohol, dehydration, and other wine compounds are more likely culprits). Sensitivity is uncommon and affects a small percentage of people with asthma, who may experience breathing symptoms.
